join_order.notes: complete_cast is the smallest fact (135K). Single linear scan filters via cct1/cct2 dim ids; skip nullable movie_id == INT32_MIN. Produces dedup set of candidate mv values.
Skip mv if production_year <= 2000 or == INT32_MIN.
Iterate mk rows for mv; require any keyword_id in k_ids (tiny set, linear scan ok).
Capture mi.info slice for MIN aggregation; length prefilter then equality.
For each surviving ci row, fetch pid; gather n.name slice for MIN.

data_structures.k_ids: flat_hash_set<int32> (<=7 entries; or sorted small array + linear scan)
data_structures.candidate_mv: no materialization required — process each surviving cc row inline; optional flat_hash_set<int32> dedup since cc may have multiple rows per movie
data_structures.mv_dedup: flat_hash_set<int32> sized ~16K to dedup movie_id across cc filter survivors
data_structures.aggregation: four std::string_view running minima (mi.info, mi_idx.info, n.name, t.title); compare via std::string_view::operator<

parallelism.notes: Partition driver scan over complete_cast (135086 rows / 12 threads). Per-thread local min strings and local mv_dedup set; merge at end with 4-way lex-min reduction.

indexes.purpose: not used for driver (linear scan), retained for sanity

aggregation: scalar_min_4way (no group-by; four global MIN aggregates merged across threads)
execution_notes: Driver order chosen because complete_cast (135K) is smallest fact and cct1/cct2 cut it ~95%.

Per surviving mv, evaluate cheap filters first: title.production_year, then movie_keyword (~2% selectivity), then movie_info Horror/Thriller, then movie_info_idx votes, finally cast_info (most expensive due to person_id chase and gender lookup).
Short-circuit each semi-join: stop on first matching row but still capture min candidate; for mi.info and mi_idx.info we must iterate all matching rows to compute MIN slice.
Skip slot 0 (NULL bucket) in offsets_only indexes.
Use string_view for varlen MIN aggregates to avoid string copies until thread-merge.
